A.text: Dietary assessment belongs at both the initial and the recurring visits, and it matters especially for caries risk.

cites.section: Policy on Nutrition and Dietary Counseling in the Pediatric Dental Setting › Background

B.text: Assessment is not limited to the first visit; it is also an important part of recurring visits.

cites.section: Policy on Nutrition and Dietary Counseling in the Pediatric Dental Setting › Background

C.text: The first visit is explicitly included as a time for assessing feeding and nutrition, so waiting for recurring visits is incorrect.

cites.section: Policy on Nutrition and Dietary Counseling in the Pediatric Dental Setting › Background

D.text: Assessment is a routine part of first and recurring visits, particularly for judging caries risk, so it should not wait until caries is already present.

cites.section: Policy on Nutrition and Dietary Counseling in the Pediatric Dental Setting › Background

explanation.text: Feeding habits and nutritional intake should be assessed at the first visit and at recurring visits, especially because of their bearing on caries risk.
